title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Flat-pack and fixture installation
audience: Flat-pack and fixture installation operators who assemble furniture, mount televisions and shelving, and hang fixtures in homes, rentals and small offices.
learningOutcomes: Write a visit offer that names the items, the fixings, the exclusions and the return-visit term
Show what certainty and protection the price includes, and what it leaves to a licensed tradesperson
Price the offer from value and cost, then compare it with published vendor ranges

instruction.heading: Sell a finished list, not a labour rate
instruction.body: A flat-pack customer buys a built item that works, mounted safely, and the certainty that the job will be finished in one visit with the right fixings. An offer such as 'we assemble up to four listed items and mount up to two wall items in one visit, check the fixings, and photograph each finished item' gives the customer a result they can see. Queensland vendor estimates give TV wall mounting at $80 to $200 and basic furniture assembly at $80 to $200 per job (The Quote Yard, QLD, published 10 May 2026). These are vendor estimates, not regulator data, and they are a check on your own prices.

instruction.heading: Use three levels that each add something visible
instruction.body: A good level might be one or two items. A better level might be up to four items in one visit with a fixings check. A best level might be a landlord-ready block of up to six items with a checklist, a photo record and a return visit for any listed item not finished. Set the prices from your own cost. Use the vendor per-job ranges, such as basic shelving at $100 to $250 (vendor), only as a check on each level.

instruction.heading: Say what you will not do
instruction.body: State the exclusions. Electrical work, such as light fittings, power points and cable runs, and plumbing work are excluded. Vendor sources say electrical and plumbing work must be done by licensed tradespeople, and they disagree about which handyman tasks need a licence. Refer those items to a licensed tradesperson and say so in the offer. The research did not find a government source that settles which light-fitting or power-point tasks need a licence, so do not state that as settled.

instruction.heading: Written terms and approval before extra work
instruction.body: A written quote binds once it is accepted, so list the items, the fixings you supply, the items the customer supplies, and the exclusions. Show one total and say whether GST is included. Extra work needs the customer's permission first. Western Australian guidance says a tradesperson cannot do extra work and then ask for payment later.

instruction.heading: Guarantees you can keep
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees for services apply and cannot be removed by contract. A return visit within a stated period for an item you fitted is a guarantee you control. Set the period from your own experience, and do not promise to repair a wall, a fitting or a product defect that the manufacturer covers.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a customer would repeat, such as 'the wardrobe is built, the TV is safely mounted, and you are ready to use the room tonight'.
List each item, the fixings you supply, and the items the customer supplies.
Write the exclusions, including electrical and plumbing work, and the referral route for those items.
Add one certainty element, such as a fixings check and a photo of each finished item, and set the return-visit period.
Set each level's price from your cost, check it against the vendor ranges for the same items, and state GST status.
Confirm the offer in writing and record it.

workedExamples.situation: A landlord asks for a TV wall mount in a rental, the assembly of a wardrobe, and a light fitting swap. The scenario is illustrative.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which level should the operator offer, what is referred out, and what price basis is shown?
workedExamples.reasoning: The operator offers the better level, covering the TV mount and the wardrobe assembly, with a fixings check and a photo of each finished item. The light fitting is referred to a licensed electrician, and the offer says so in writing. Vendor estimates for the two items in Queensland are TV wall mounting at $80 to $200 and basic furniture assembly at $80 to $200 (The Quote Yard, 10 May 2026). Added together, the two ranges give $160 to $400 (illustrative arithmetic). The vendor page does not price a light fitting, so no figure is given for it. The operator sets the total from his own cost and margin, not from those ranges, and shows one total with GST status.

equipmentAndPpe: Offer template with items, fixings supplied, customer-supplied items and exclusions
Photo checklist for each finished item
Fixings list with the wall type recorded where the customer has confirmed it
PPE as set by the site's own rules and {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Bundling electrical work into a flat-pack or fixture visit
commonErrors.prevention: Exclude electrical and plumbing work in writing, and refer it to a licensed tradesperson.

commonErrors.error: Fixing to a wall without a fixings check or a record of the wall type
commonErrors.prevention: Check the fixings and record the wall type where the customer has confirmed it.

commonErrors.error: Promising a result that depends on a product defect or a wall you have not inspected
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to a return visit for your own work, and exclude manufacturer defects.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited. Show one total with GST status. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority.

Electrical and plumbing work requires a licensed tradesperson. Vendor sources (Airtasker, Lawpath and The Quote Yard) say so, and Airtasker's Victorian section lists electricity and plumbing as needing a licence regardless of cost, while its FAQ says handyman licences are not usually required. The government source that would settle the position for light fittings and power points was not retrieved. Check with the state electrical regulator before doing any task near wiring.

Insurance thresholds, not licences: in Queensland, kitchen or bathroom fixtures and fittings, and windows and doors, need home-warranty cover when the project cost is more than $3,300 including GST. A standalone fixture is unlikely to exceed that on its own, but a bundled kitchen or bathroom job could.

qualityStandard: Every offer lists its items, fixings, exclusions and return-visit term.
Every quote shows one total with GST status and a validity date.
Every electrical or plumbing item is excluded in writing and referred to a licensed tradesperson.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with items, fixings, exclusions and time frame
Record of any referred item and the licensed tradesperson it was referred to
summary: Sell a finished list, with the fixings checked and the exclusions stated.
Refer electrical and plumbing work to a licensed tradesperson, and say so in the offer.
Show one total, the exclusions and the GST status.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a flat-pack offer does the customer buy?
options: Your hourly rate on its own
A built, working item with the fixings checked, in one visit
How many years you have been in business

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks you to swap a light fitting during a flat-pack visit. What should the offer say?
options: That you will do it at the same price as the shelves
That electrical work is excluded and will be referred to a licensed tradesperson
That you will do it quietly and not put it in writing
That the light fitting is included at no extra charge

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee in a flat-pack offer be?
options: Unlimited and open-ended, including manufacturer defects
Something you can deliver and afford, such as a return visit for your own work
Impossible to claim on in any case
Available only to friends of the business

officialReferences.covers: As summarised in the research file: misleading statements about prices are prohibited, and a total price with GST status is the safer way to show a price. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: The Quote Yard, Handyman services QLD, https://www.thequoteyard.com.au/services/handyman-services-qld, published 10 May 2026. Vendor estimates for TV wall mounting, basic shelving, basic furniture assembly and picture hanging; states that electrical and plumbing work needs licensed tradespeople.

Airtasker, 'Tasker handyman licence' guide (AU), https://www.airtasker.com/au/guides/tasker-handyman-licence/, last updated 13 March 2024. Vendor; states licence rules by state; its own FAQ conflicts with its state sections.

Lawpath, 'How to start a handyman business', https://lawpath.com.au/blog/how-to-start-a-handyman-business, dated 19 October 2026 per byline. Vendor legal blog; electrical and plumbing work needs a licence.
QBCC, 'Home warranty cover', https://www.qbcc.qld.gov.au/node/2886, last reviewed 1 August 2024. Kitchen or bathroom fixtures and windows and doors above $3,300 including GST.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Due care and skill; reasonable chance to fix a minor fault.
business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. A written quote becomes binding once accepted.
WA Consumer Protection, 'Estimates, quotes and deposits', https://consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/estimates-quotes-and-deposits, last updated 4 September 2026. Extra work needs permission first.
